# Quarto {#sec-quarto}

::: {.callout-note title="Why this matters"}
Your submission requires both a reproducible report and a set of
presentation slides — Quarto builds both from the same kind of source file.
It runs your R code and inserts the real output every time you render, so
you never copy-paste a number or a plot in by hand.
:::

The starter template (@sec-starter-template) already includes both:
`docs/report.qmd` for the written report and `docs/slides.qmd` for
presentation slides.

## Anatomy of a `.qmd` file

````markdown
---
title: "Team Name — Datathon Submission"
author: "Team Name"
format: html
---

# Introduction

We analyse the AI Incident Database to answer...

```{{r}}
library(tidyverse)
summary(cars)
```
````

- Text outside code chunks is normal Markdown.
- Anything inside ```` ```{r} ``` ```` blocks runs at render time.
- Add `#| echo: false` inside a chunk to keep the output but hide the code —
  useful for staying within a word limit.

## Render your report

- RStudio/Positron: click **Render**, or press `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+K`.
- Command line:
  ```bash
  quarto render report.qmd            # render using the format in the YAML
  quarto render report.qmd --to pdf   # force a specific format
  quarto preview report.qmd           # live preview, reloads on save
  ```

Use `quarto preview` while you write — it catches broken chunks immediately
instead of at the end.

## Set your output format

Both HTML **and** PDF are required for the report — list both formats in
the YAML and Quarto renders one file for each:

```yaml
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    code-fold: true   # readers can expand/collapse code blocks
  pdf:
    documentclass: article
```

```bash
quarto render report.qmd   # produces report.html and report.pdf
```

The report has a **3,000-word limit**, excluding code, tables, figure
captions, and references.

## Build presentation slides (required from every team)

A finished slide deck is part of your submission, not an optional extra —
every team builds one, even though only the 5 finalists actually present it
live (2:15–3:30 PM, Day 2: 10 min talk + 5 min Q&A each). Treat it with the
same care as the report: it's judged on Professional Communication just
like everything else you submit.

```yaml
---
title: "Team Name — Datathon Presentation"
format: revealjs
---
```

1. Start each new slide with a `##` heading.
2. Write R chunks exactly as you would in the report — plots and tables
   render live into the deck.
3. Render the same way: **Render** button, `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+K`, or
   `quarto render slides.qmd`.
4. Open the resulting `.html` in a browser; press `f` for fullscreen, use
   arrow keys or space to advance.

````markdown
## Introduction

The question we investigated...

## Our Approach

```{{r}}
ggplot(data, aes(x, y)) + geom_point()
```

## Results

Key finding...
````

## Set up PDF rendering (before the event)

Since PDF is a required output, don't leave this until Day 2. PDF needs
LaTeX — install it once, ahead of time:

```r
install.packages("tinytex")
tinytex::install_tinytex()
```

Render both formats and open both files before the deadline — a report
that renders fine to HTML can still fail on PDF (e.g. an image or table
that doesn't fit the page).

## Keep the report reproducible and inside the word limit

1. Render early and often — don't wait until the deadline to find a broken
   chunk.
2. Decide how much code you want visible in the final report — the `echo`,
   `warning`, and `message` options (set per chunk, or globally under
   `execute:` in the YAML) control this. There's no required setup here;
   choose whatever makes your report read cleanly.
3. Cache slow steps (a MongoDB pull, a model fit) with `#| cache: true` on
   that chunk.
4. Use `knitr::kable()` or `gt` for tables, and pipe large printed output
   through `head()` — raw tibble/model printouts can quietly blow out your
   word count.
5. Keep the raw `.qmd` in your GitHub repo, not just the rendered file — the
   repo is what gets checked for reproducibility.
